governance_posts.title: [ARFC] Expand Coinbase Tokenized Equities on Base
governance_posts.description:
Summary

This ARFC proposes to expand the Aave V4 Equities Hub on Base with six Coinbase tokenized equities as collateral: Netflix (NFLXc), Oracle (ORCLc), Palantir Technologies (PLTRc), Advanced Micro Devices (AMDc), ServiceNow (NOWc), and Strategy (MSTRc). The first five are S&P 500 constituents and Strategy is listed on Nasdaq outside the index. All six are issued on the same Base stack as the Magnificent Seven (Mag7) tokens already on the hub, namely the B20 token standard and Coinbase’s Token Supply Manager, and are to be priced by Chainlink total return feeds on the 24/5 template of the existing reserves. MSTRc’s feed is already live. They would join the Mag-7 Spoke as collateral only, with USDC as the borrowable asset, under the same market structure as the existing reserves.

Reserve Volatility, 1 year Collateral Factor Max Liquidation Bonus Add Cap
NFLXc 36.2% 71% 5.50% 79,038 (USD 5.00M)
ORCLc 59.2% 58% 5.50% 42,378 (USD 5.00M)
PLTRc 58.9% 58% 5.50% 29,617 (USD 5.00M)
AMDc 72.9% 49% 5.50% 9,704 (USD 5.00M)
NOWc 66.7% 50% 5.50% 50,195 (USD 5.00M)
MSTRc 81.1% 47% 6.50% 41,298 (USD 5.00M)

Source: LlamaRisk, November 12, 2026

The six stocks trade between USD 1.8B and 10.9B a day in their cash markets, and all six have perpetual markets on Binance, Hyperliquid, and OKX. The more volatile a stock, the lower its collateral factor. NFLX moves about as much as the Mag7 stocks already on the hub, whose volatility ranges from 25.0% to 46.3%, while ORCL, PLTR, AMD, NOW and MSTR move more than any of them. The maximum liquidation bonus is 5.5% on the first five, the same as the Mag7 reserves on the spoke, and 6.5% on MSTRc, which also carries a 10% risk premium. The add caps are set at USD 5M of collateral per token, USD 30.0M in total, and the spoke’s unchanged USDC draw cap of USD 21M bounds what the hub’s USDC suppliers lend against the equities on the spoke.

Motivation

The Equities Hub currently holds eight tokenized equities alongside USDC. Onboarding the six tokens would:

  • Broaden the collateral on the hub with large-cap US equities whose cash markets trade between USD 1.8B and 10.9B a day.
  • Add collateral issued under the same program, token standard, and price feed design as the existing reserves, so that the market structure, liquidation routes, and oracle setup of the hub apply without change.
  • Allow borrowers on the pooled spoke to hold more diversified collateral positions, with each asset keeping its own collateral factor.

1. The Six Stocks

Five of the six are S&P 500 constituents. Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, is listed on Nasdaq and is not a member of the index. All six have trading histories back to 2018 or earlier, except Palantir, which listed in September 2020. Each clears the listing floor of USD 2B of market capitalization and USD 50M of median daily traded value by a factor of 25 or more, and none of the six reports substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern in its latest annual or quarterly report.

Token Company Listing Market cap Daily traded value, 63-session median Dividend Quarterly results
NFLXc Netflix Nasdaq USD 259.8B USD 2.4B None Reported 2026-10-20, next expected January 2027
ORCLc Oracle NYSE USD 366.9B USD 3.8B Quarterly, USD 0.50 Reported 2026-09-10, next expected December 2026
PLTRc Palantir Technologies Nasdaq USD 406.8B USD 4.4B None Reported 2026-11-02, next expected February 2027
AMDc Advanced Micro Devices Nasdaq USD 845.0B USD 10.9B None Reported 2026-11-03, next expected February 2027
NOWc ServiceNow NYSE USD 103.4B USD 1.8B None Reported 2026-10-28, next expected January 2027
MSTRc Strategy Nasdaq USD 51.1B USD 2.7B None Reported 2026-10-29, next expected February 2027

Source: SEC EDGAR and Yahoo Finance, November 10, 2026

Market capitalization counts every share class at the close of November 10, 2026. Daily traded value is the median daily dollar volume over the 63 sessions to the same date.

Oracle is the only one of the six that pays a dividend on its common stock. Strategy pays dividends on its preferred stock only. Dividends and other corporate actions reach the tokens through the issuer multiplier, as described in Section 4 of the technical review. The ORCLc multiplier stands at 1.00004, set on October 23, 2026, the pay date of Oracle’s last dividend. Oracle’s next dividend has not been declared. None of the six companies has announced a split, a spin-off, a tender offer, a delisting, or a merger in which it is the target.

Strategy held 848,517 bitcoin on October 25, 2026, worth USD 68.3B, more than its market capitalization. Its convertible notes (USD 6.7B) and preferred stock (about USD 14.1B of liquidation preference) rank ahead of the Class A shares the token tracks, according to its quarterly report for the quarter to September 30, 2026.

2. Price Behavior

Volatility is the annualized standard deviation of daily close-to-close log returns. The drawdown is the largest peak-to-trough fall of the closing price. Earnings nights are the nights with a quarterly results filing among each stock’s ten largest falls from a close to the next open since 2019.

Stock Volatility, 1 year Volatility, 30 sessions Worst day since 2018 Largest drawdown, 1 year Earnings nights among the 10 worst
NFLX 36.2% 34.5% -35.1% -46.4% 8
ORCL 59.2% 70.1% -13.8% -53.7% 6
PLTR 58.9% 55.8% -21.3% -44.8% 6
AMD 72.9% 97.1% -17.3% -37.7% 3
NOW 66.7% 100.7% -27.0% -52.2% 4
MSTR 81.1% 71.6% -25.5% -65.5% 0
Mag7 range 25.0% to 46.3% 23.0% to 52.2% -12.6% to -26.4% -13.8% to -39.1% 2 to 7

Source: Yahoo Finance and SEC EDGAR, November 10, 2026

ORCL, PLTR, AMD, NOW and MSTR moved with annualized volatility of 58.9% to 81.1% over the past year, above TSLA at 46.3%, the most volatile of the Mag7. MSTR is the most volatile of the six. NFLX, at 36.2%, sits within the Mag7 range. Over the last 30 sessions AMD and NOW rose to 97.1% and 100.7%, after their quarterly results on November 3 and October 28, 2026.

NOW’s worst day since 2018 was its results session of October 29, 2026, a fall of 27.0%. Earnings nights account for three to eight of the ten largest falls from a close to the next open for each of the first five, so their largest overnight moves cluster around scheduled quarterly releases. Six of MSTR’s ten largest falls came over weekends, when bitcoin trades and the stock does not, and none on a results night. ORCL, NOW and MSTR also fell 53.7%, 52.2% and 65.5% from peak to trough over the past year.


Source: Yahoo Finance, November 10, 2026

Each of the six feeds is expected to meet these requirements, as MSTRc’s live feed does:

  • It prices the token as the underlying share price times the issuer multiplier, as on the listed reserves.
  • It publishes through the pre-market, regular, post-market and overnight sessions, from Sunday 20:00 to Friday 20:00 ET.
  • It updates on a deviation threshold of at most 0.5%, the oracle allowance in the collateral factor, and a heartbeat of at most 24 hours within those sessions.

The feeds stop updating from Friday 20:00 to Sunday 20:00 ET and on US market holidays, and keep showing the last price. Positions can still be liquidated in that window, but only at that price, so a move in the stock over the weekend reaches positions when the feed restarts on Sunday evening.

3. Perpetual Futures

Perpetual futures let a liquidator hedge seized collateral while the cash market is closed. All six names trade on Binance, Hyperliquid, and OKX, and all except NFLX on Lighter. Open interest is counted once per contract on every venue, so Hyperliquid’s reported figure, which sums long and short positions, is halved.

On November 11, 2026 open interest across the four venues ranged from USD 3.05M (NOW) to USD 42.07M (AMD) on the first five, and 24-hour volume from USD 2.64M (NOW) to USD 441.07M (AMD). MSTR carried USD 111.17M of open interest and USD 362.25M of 24-hour volume on November 12, 2026, more open interest than any Mag7 name except GOOGL and NVDA. Only AMD and MSTR exceed the smallest Mag7 total, USD 33.52M on AMZN, while the largest, NVDA, carries USD 543.06M. Binance holds the largest share of open interest on all six names. Turnover relative to open interest is highest on AMD, at about 10.5 times its open interest in a day.

Perpetual markets on MSTR, AMD and ORCL are deep enough to hedge a large liquidation. A quarter of a full USD 5M cap is about 1.1% of MSTR’s open interest. On PLTR, NFLX and NOW they are thinner, so a hedge of a quarter of a full cap, USD 1.25M, would move their price, especially at weekends. The hedge is not needed to protect the market: the collateral factor covers the fall until the next regular session, when seized tokens can be redeemed or sold, and the cap limits the amount at risk to USD 5M per token.


Source: Binance, Hyperliquid, OKX and Lighter, November 11, 2026

Over the last 30 days, median weekday volume across the four venues ranged from USD 3.3M (NOW) to USD 345.9M (MSTR), with weekend volume at a ninth to about a fifth of weekday levels. Open interest on Binance and OKX roughly halved on PLTR (USD 16.7M to 8.9M), eased on ORCL (USD 25.7M to 17.6M), held steady on NFLX (USD 7.0M to 6.9M), and ended level on AMD (USD 29.1M to 28.3M) after a peak of USD 56.2M around its results. On NOW it rose from USD 1.6M to 1.9M, after a peak of about USD 5.5M in the session after its results, and on MSTR from USD 92.7M to 99.0M.


*Source: Binance, Hyperliquid, **OKX *and Lighter, October 12 to November 10, 2026


Source: Binance and OKX, October 12 to November 10, 2026

4. The Tokens on Base

Each token is a CB Certificate issued by Coinbase Onchain SPV Ltd under a series prospectus approved by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Abu Dhabi Global Market between September 3 and October 7, 2026 (NFLXc, ORCLc, PLTRc, AMDc, NOWc, MSTRc). Apart from the series details, the description of the underlying issuer, and minor drafting changes, the NFLXc, ORCLc, PLTRc, AMDc and NOWc prospectuses carry the text of the SpaceX prospectus of September 3, 2026, whose terms and conditions and deed of trust are those of the NVIDIA series examined in the technical review and the SPCXc assessment. The MSTRc prospectus, approved the same day as SpaceX’s, differs from it in the series details only. The tokens use the same B20 standard and Token Supply Manager as the listed reserves, and their admin, operator, pause, metadata, mint, and burn roles are held by the same addresses as on the listed Coinbase tokens.

Anyone who acquires the tokens on the secondary market, a liquidator included, holds them as an unvested holder, with no redemption right until it completes the issuer’s vesting process. The issuer’s operator can change a token’s multiplier by any amount in one transaction, and the feed carries the new value into the price at its next update. Announced corporate actions run with the issuer’s registry pause, during which the feed holds its last value and minting and redemption stop. The six reserves take this price setup on the same terms as the listed Coinbase reserves.

Token Series prospectus First mint Supply Mints / redemptions Mint allowance per 24h DEX depth at 2% impact Multiplier
NFLXc 2026-09-24 2026-09-24 7,953.59 (USD 503k) 104 / 41 70,100 (USD 4.43M) USD 203k 1.00000
ORCLc 2026-09-25 2026-09-28 3,073.19 (USD 363k) 87 / 36 35,800 (USD 4.22M) USD 129k 1.00004
PLTRc 2026-09-24 2026-09-24 2,879.10 (USD 486k) 213 / 204 26,100 (USD 4.41M) USD 148k 1.00000
AMDc 2026-09-25 2026-09-28 1,059.92 (USD 546k) 105 / 44 7,900 (USD 4.07M) USD 212k 1.00000
NOWc 2026-10-07 Not minted 0 0 / 0 36,200 (USD 3.61M) None 1.00000
MSTRc 2026-09-03 2026-09-03 19,506.98 (USD 2.36M) 731 / 517 40,800 (USD 4.94M) USD 230k 1.00000

Source: Basescan and KyberSwap, November 11, 2026

The daily mint allowance of each token is sized to USD 3.6M to 4.4M of notional per 24 hours on the first five and USD 4.9M on MSTRc, against USD 4.1M to 5.5M for the Mag7 tokens. The tokens carry no supply cap, and the minter’s 24-hour allowance is the only limit on new supply, which the issuance administrator can raise in one transaction. The add caps bound the hub’s exposure to each token whatever its supply. Supply stands between USD 363k and 546k per minted token of the first five, and NOWc has not yet been minted. MSTRc’s supply of USD 2.36M lies within the Mag7 range of USD 1.40M to 10.27M, and it carries the most primary activity, with 731 mints and 517 redemptions since September 3, 2026.

Secondary liquidity on Base for the first five is thinner than on the listed tokens. Between USD 129k and 212k of each minted token sells into USDC within a 2% price impact, against USD 246k (TSLAc) to 569k (AMZNc) for the Mag7 tokens. Each of the four minted tokens among them sells through a single Aerodrome Slipstream pool, whose liquidity range runs out before the price moves 2%. NOWc has no pool with usable depth. MSTRc sells USD 230k within 2%, inside the Mag7 range, across several Aerodrome pools and request-for-quote market makers.

5. Parameters

The six reserves join the pooled lending spoke of the Equities Hub on the same terms as the existing collateral: collateral only, a 10% liquidation fee, receive-shares enabled, and a collateral risk of 0, or 10% on MSTRc.

5.1 Collateral Factor

In Aave V4 the collateral factor is both the borrowing limit and the liquidation threshold. For a stock priced 24/5, it has to cover the largest fall from any off-hours price to the lowest price before five minutes past the next regular open, plus a 0.5% allowance for the feed’s deviation threshold. It is sized so that this fall exceeds a stock’s haircut on one night per stock in ten years, with a 2020-type crash counted as one year in ten.

The haircut scales a forecast of the stock’s daily volatility over the next year by the size of a once-in-ten-years off-hours fall relative to daily volatility, measured across S&P 500 stocks. The forecast weights the stock’s recent moves and pulls them partly toward the market-wide level. The collateral factor is what remains after the haircut, the maximum liquidation bonus and an allowance for interest while a position waits for liquidation, rounded down to a whole point.

Reserve Daily returns Recent volatility, annualized Haircut Collateral factor
NFLXc 6,155 35.8% 24.49% 71%
ORCLc 10,244 63.0% 38.31% 58%
PLTRc 1,534 61.7% 37.70% 58%
AMDc 11,757 82.9% 47.67% 49%
NOWc 3,610 79.6% 46.15% 50%
MSTRc 7,147 80.8% 49.28% 47%

Source: Yahoo Finance, November 10, 2026

NFLXc carries the highest collateral factor of the six, with recent volatility of 35.8% a year. AMDc and NOWc sit at the low end, as their results nights of November 3-4 and October 28-29, 2026 took their recent volatility to 82.9% and 79.6% a year. MSTRc carries the lowest, 47%, although its recent volatility of 80.8% sits between theirs. Strategy is not an S&P 500 member, so its haircut uses the larger scale the method sets for stocks outside the index.

The collateral factors are set in full at listing and then reviewed with every listed stock at the last session of December, with a lower factor phased in over 10 sessions. The interest allowance charges 24% a year over the longest market closure, 92 hours and 35 minutes. That is the top of the hub’s USDC rate curve, so it covers the full curve.


*Source: **Aave *and Yahoo Finance, November 11, 2026

5.2 Liquidation Bonus

The maximum liquidation bonus is 5.5% on the first five, the value of the Mag7 reserves on the spoke, kept until the market has a longer liquidation history. MSTRc carries 6.5%, one point more, as SPCXc does, since its weekend gaps reach positions all at once when the feed reopens. Liquidators are relied on to liquidate positions and rotate the seized tokens within about 30 minutes in the US regular session. The spoke’s bonus curve pays 90% of the maximum at a health factor of 1.0 and the full maximum from a health factor of 0.90, so the first five pay 4.95% at a health factor of 1.0 and 5.5% from 0.90, and MSTRc 5.85% and 6.5%. At a health factor just below 1.0 the liquidator keeps about 4.46% of the repaid debt after the protocol’s 10% share, 5.27% on MSTRc, against the 2.6% a hedge costs in the regular session.

A liquidator with redemption access, a vested holder or an authorised participant, can redeem seized tokens through the issuer during regular hours. A liquidator without it sells on Base or hedges with a perpetual short until it can sell. With secondary depth of USD 129k to 230k at a 2% price impact, liquidations beyond small sizes go through redemption or a perpetual hedge.

5.3 Caps

The caps limit the size a liquidator may have to absorb. Each add cap starts at USD 5M of collateral, rises with the supply on the reserve to keep room for new deposits, and never exceeds the stock’s median daily traded value over the last 63 sessions, USD 1.8B to 10.9B for these six. The token counts below are at the close of November 10, 2026. The caps are reviewed daily after listing.

Reserve Hard cap, 63-session median daily traded value DEX depth at 2% impact Token supply Add cap Add cap, USD
NFLXc USD 2.43B USD 203k 7,953.59 (USD 503k) 79,038 USD 5.00M
ORCLc USD 3.82B USD 129k 3,073.19 (USD 363k) 42,378 USD 5.00M
PLTRc USD 4.37B USD 148k 2,879.10 (USD 486k) 29,617 USD 5.00M
AMDc USD 10.87B USD 212k 1,059.92 (USD 546k) 9,704 USD 5.00M
NOWc USD 1.82B None 0 50,195 USD 5.00M
MSTRc USD 2.74B USD 230k 19,506.98 (USD 2.36M) 41,298 USD 5.00M

Source: Yahoo Finance, Basescan and KyberSwap, November 11, 2026

At a hard cap of one day’s trading, a quarter of a capped supply liquidated at once and sold at a quarter of the market’s pace fits in one regular session. For these six, a quarter of USD 5M is USD 1.25M, against USD 1.8B to 10.9B traded each day on US venues.

Together the caps amount to USD 30.0M of collateral, which supports USD 16.6M of USDC debt at the proposed collateral factors. The caps on NFLXc, ORCLc, PLTRc and AMDc are 9 to 14 times each token’s supply on November 11, 2026, NOWc has no supply, and MSTRc’s cap is 2.1 times its supply. The issuer mints tokens on demand, and supply may follow the collateral demand of the market. USDC debt on the spoke stood at USD 7.01M on November 11, 2026, against the 21M USDC draw cap, and the USDC caps on the spoke are unchanged.

5.4 Risk Premium

MSTRc carries a collateral risk of 10%, while the other five stay at 0, as do the Mag7. The premium raises the borrow rate only on the part of a borrower’s debt that relies on MSTRc.

Specification

Market Composition

The six reserves join the Mag-7 Spoke, which holds the seven Magnificent Seven tokens and SPCXc as collateral, with USDC as the only borrowable asset. A user can post any combination of the fourteen tokens and borrow USDC against it, with each token counted at its own collateral factor. The equities are collateral only.

Spoke Parameters

The liquidation fee is 10%, as on the listed reserves. Collateral risk is 0 for the first five and 10% for MSTRc, the spoke’s USDC reserve carries a risk premium threshold of 1,100%, and liquidators can receive collateral as shares on every reserve.

Dynamic Liquidation Bonus Configuration

Price Feeds

2. Price Behavior

Volatility is the annualized standard deviation of daily close-to-close log returns. The drawdown is the largest peak-to-trough fall of the closing price. Earnings nights are the nights with a quarterly results filing among each stock’s ten largest falls from a close to the next open since 2019.

NOW’s worst day since 2018 was its results session of October 29, 2026, a fall of 27.0%. Earnings nights account for three to eight of the ten largest falls from a close to the next open for each of the first five, so their largest overnight moves cluster around scheduled quarterly releases. Six of MSTR’s ten largest falls came over weekends, when bitcoin trades and the stock does not, and none on a results night. ORCL, NOW and MSTR also fell 53.7%, 52.2% and 65.5% from peak to trough over the past year.


Source: Yahoo Finance, November 10, 2026

Each of the six feeds is expected to meet these requirements, as MSTRc’s live feed does:

  • It prices the token as the underlying share price times the issuer multiplier, as on the listed reserves.
  • It publishes through the pre-market, regular, post-market and overnight sessions, from Sunday 20:00 to Friday 20:00 ET.
  • It updates on a deviation threshold of at most 0.5%, the oracle allowance in the collateral factor, and a heartbeat of at most 24 hours within those sessions.

The feeds stop updating from Friday 20:00 to Sunday 20:00 ET and on US market holidays, and keep showing the last price. Positions can still be liquidated in that window, but only at that price, so a move in the stock over the weekend reaches positions when the feed restarts on Sunday evening.

3. Perpetual Futures

Perpetual futures let a liquidator hedge seized collateral while the cash market is closed. All six names trade on Binance, Hyperliquid, and OKX, and all except NFLX on Lighter. Open interest is counted once per contract on every venue, so Hyperliquid’s reported figure, which sums long and short positions, is halved.

On November 11, 2026 open interest across the four venues ranged from USD 3.05M (NOW) to USD 42.07M (AMD) on the first five, and 24-hour volume from USD 2.64M (NOW) to USD 441.07M (AMD). MSTR carried USD 111.17M of open interest and USD 362.25M of 24-hour volume on November 12, 2026, more open interest than any Mag7 name except GOOGL and NVDA. Only AMD and MSTR exceed the smallest Mag7 total, USD 33.52M on AMZN, while the largest, NVDA, carries USD 543.06M. Binance holds the largest share of open interest on all six names. Turnover relative to open interest is highest on AMD, at about 10.5 times its open interest in a day.

Perpetual markets on MSTR, AMD and ORCL are deep enough to hedge a large liquidation. A quarter of a full USD 5M cap is about 1.1% of MSTR’s open interest. On PLTR, NFLX and NOW they are thinner, so a hedge of a quarter of a full cap, USD 1.25M, would move their price, especially at weekends. The hedge is not needed to protect the market: the collateral factor covers the fall until the next regular session, when seized tokens can be redeemed or sold, and the cap limits the amount at risk to USD 5M per token.


Source: Binance, Hyperliquid, OKX and Lighter, November 11, 2026

Over the last 30 days, median weekday volume across the four venues ranged from USD 3.3M (NOW) to USD 345.9M (MSTR), with weekend volume at a ninth to about a fifth of weekday levels. Open interest on Binance and OKX roughly halved on PLTR (USD 16.7M to 8.9M), eased on ORCL (USD 25.7M to 17.6M), held steady on NFLX (USD 7.0M to 6.9M), and ended level on AMD (USD 29.1M to 28.3M) after a peak of USD 56.2M around its results. On NOW it rose from USD 1.6M to 1.9M, after a peak of about USD 5.5M in the session after its results, and on MSTR from USD 92.7M to 99.0M.


*Source: Binance, Hyperliquid, **OKX *and Lighter, October 12 to November 10, 2026


Source: Binance and OKX, October 12 to November 10, 2026

4. The Tokens on Base

Each token is a CB Certificate issued by Coinbase Onchain SPV Ltd under a series prospectus approved by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Abu Dhabi Global Market between September 3 and October 7, 2026 (NFLXc, ORCLc, PLTRc, AMDc, NOWc, MSTRc). Apart from the series details, the description of the underlying issuer, and minor drafting changes, the NFLXc, ORCLc, PLTRc, AMDc and NOWc prospectuses carry the text of the SpaceX prospectus of September 3, 2026, whose terms and conditions and deed of trust are those of the NVIDIA series examined in the technical review and the SPCXc assessment. The MSTRc prospectus, approved the same day as SpaceX’s, differs from it in the series details only. The tokens use the same B20 standard and Token Supply Manager as the listed reserves, and their admin, operator, pause, metadata, mint, and burn roles are held by the same addresses as on the listed Coinbase tokens.

Anyone who acquires the tokens on the secondary market, a liquidator included, holds them as an unvested holder, with no redemption right until it completes the issuer’s vesting process. The issuer’s operator can change a token’s multiplier by any amount in one transaction, and the feed carries the new value into the price at its next update. Announced corporate actions run with the issuer’s registry pause, during which the feed holds its last value and minting and redemption stop. The six reserves take this price setup on the same terms as the listed Coinbase reserves.

The daily mint allowance of each token is sized to USD 3.6M to 4.4M of notional per 24 hours on the first five and USD 4.9M on MSTRc, against USD 4.1M to 5.5M for the Mag7 tokens. The tokens carry no supply cap, and the minter’s 24-hour allowance is the only limit on new supply, which the issuance administrator can raise in one transaction. The add caps bound the hub’s exposure to each token whatever its supply. Supply stands between USD 363k and 546k per minted token of the first five, and NOWc has not yet been minted. MSTRc’s supply of USD 2.36M lies within the Mag7 range of USD 1.40M to 10.27M, and it carries the most primary activity, with 731 mints and 517 redemptions since September 3, 2026.

Secondary liquidity on Base for the first five is thinner than on the listed tokens. Between USD 129k and 212k of each minted token sells into USDC within a 2% price impact, against USD 246k (TSLAc) to 569k (AMZNc) for the Mag7 tokens. Each of the four minted tokens among them sells through a single Aerodrome Slipstream pool, whose liquidity range runs out before the price moves 2%. NOWc has no pool with usable depth. MSTRc sells USD 230k within 2%, inside the Mag7 range, across several Aerodrome pools and request-for-quote market makers.

5. Parameters

The six reserves join the pooled lending spoke of the Equities Hub on the same terms as the existing collateral: collateral only, a 10% liquidation fee, receive-shares enabled, and a collateral risk of 0, or 10% on MSTRc.

5.1 Collateral Factor

In Aave V4 the collateral factor is both the borrowing limit and the liquidation threshold. For a stock priced 24/5, it has to cover the largest fall from any off-hours price to the lowest price before five minutes past the next regular open, plus a 0.5% allowance for the feed’s deviation threshold. It is sized so that this fall exceeds a stock’s haircut on one night per stock in ten years, with a 2020-type crash counted as one year in ten.

The haircut scales a forecast of the stock’s daily volatility over the next year by the size of a once-in-ten-years off-hours fall relative to daily volatility, measured across S&P 500 stocks. The forecast weights the stock’s recent moves and pulls them partly toward the market-wide level. The collateral factor is what remains after the haircut, the maximum liquidation bonus and an allowance for interest while a position waits for liquidation, rounded down to a whole point.

ORCLc 10,244 63.0% 38.31% 58%

AMDc 11,757 82.9% 47.67% 49%
NOWc 3,610 79.6% 46.15% 50%
MSTRc 7,147 80.8% 49.28% 47%

Source: Yahoo Finance, November 10, 2026

NFLXc carries the highest collateral factor of the six, with recent volatility of 35.8% a year. AMDc and NOWc sit at the low end, as their results nights of November 3-4 and October 28-29, 2026 took their recent volatility to 82.9% and 79.6% a year. MSTRc carries the lowest, 47%, although its recent volatility of 80.8% sits between theirs. Strategy is not an S&P 500 member, so its haircut uses the larger scale the method sets for stocks outside the index.

The collateral factors are set in full at listing and then reviewed with every listed stock at the last session of December, with a lower factor phased in over 10 sessions. The interest allowance charges 24% a year over the longest market closure, 92 hours and 35 minutes. That is the top of the hub’s USDC rate curve, so it covers the full curve.


*Source: **Aave *and Yahoo Finance, November 11, 2026

5.2 Liquidation Bonus

The maximum liquidation bonus is 5.5% on the first five, the value of the Mag7 reserves on the spoke, kept until the market has a longer liquidation history. MSTRc carries 6.5%, one point more, as SPCXc does, since its weekend gaps reach positions all at once when the feed reopens. Liquidators are relied on to liquidate positions and rotate the seized tokens within about 30 minutes in the US regular session. The spoke’s bonus curve pays 90% of the maximum at a health factor of 1.0 and the full maximum from a health factor of 0.90, so the first five pay 4.95% at a health factor of 1.0 and 5.5% from 0.90, and MSTRc 5.85% and 6.5%. At a health factor just below 1.0 the liquidator keeps about 4.46% of the repaid debt after the protocol’s 10% share, 5.27% on MSTRc, against the 2.6% a hedge costs in the regular session.

A liquidator with redemption access, a vested holder or an authorised participant, can redeem seized tokens through the issuer during regular hours. A liquidator without it sells on Base or hedges with a perpetual short until it can sell. With secondary depth of USD 129k to 230k at a 2% price impact, liquidations beyond small sizes go through redemption or a perpetual hedge.

5.3 Caps

The caps limit the size a liquidator may have to absorb. Each add cap starts at USD 5M of collateral, rises with the supply on the reserve to keep room for new deposits, and never exceeds the stock’s median daily traded value over the last 63 sessions, USD 1.8B to 10.9B for these six. The token counts below are at the close of November 10, 2026. The caps are reviewed daily after listing.

At a hard cap of one day’s trading, a quarter of a capped supply liquidated at once and sold at a quarter of the market’s pace fits in one regular session. For these six, a quarter of USD 5M is USD 1.25M, against USD 1.8B to 10.9B traded each day on US venues.

Together the caps amount to USD 30.0M of collateral, which supports USD 16.6M of USDC debt at the proposed collateral factors. The caps on NFLXc, ORCLc, PLTRc and AMDc are 9 to 14 times each token’s supply on November 11, 2026, NOWc has no supply, and MSTRc’s cap is 2.1 times its supply. The issuer mints tokens on demand, and supply may follow the collateral demand of the market. USDC debt on the spoke stood at USD 7.01M on November 11, 2026, against the 21M USDC draw cap, and the USDC caps on the spoke are unchanged.

5.4 Risk Premium

MSTRc carries a collateral risk of 10%, while the other five stay at 0, as do the Mag7. The premium raises the borrow rate only on the part of a borrower’s debt that relies on MSTRc.

governance_posts.title: Risk Stewards: Cap and IRM Changes on Aave V3 / 2026.11.18
governance_posts.description:
Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 Core:

  • Increase supply cap for WBTC from 35,500 to 36,000.
  • Increase borrow cap for USDT from 2,560,000,000 to 2,700,000,000.
  • Reduce borrow cap for USDC from 2,950,000,000 to 2,700,000,000.

Aave V3 Horizon:

  • Reduce supply cap for USCC from 7,500,000 to 3,000,000.
  • Reduce supply cap for USTB from 8,000,000 to 2,000,000.

Stablecoin IRM:

  • Increase Slope 1 by 10 BPS on 11 stablecoin reserves across Aave V3 Core, Base, Avalanche, Optimism, Plasma, Monad and Mantle, reduce Slope 1 for EURC on Aave V3 Base from 7.50% to 7.00%, and raise the optimal utilization point for USDC on Aave V3 Base from 90% to 92%.

Other IRM:

  • Increase Slope 1 for USDC on Aave V3 Arbitrum from 4.30% to 4.40% and raise the optimal utilization point from 90% to 92%.
  • For USD₮0 on Aave V3 X Layer, increase Slope 1 from 4.50% to 5.00%, reduce Slope 2 from 20.00% to 10.00%, and raise the optimal utilization point from 90% to 92%.
  • Increase the base variable borrow rate for USDe on Aave V3 Mantle from 6.60% to 7.00%.

WBTC (Aave V3 Core)

WBTC has reached 98.4% supply cap utilization (34,938 / 35,500) on the Aave V3 Core instance.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, November 18, 2026

The top 20 WBTC suppliers run health factors between 1.17 and 6.03 with a median of 1.72, with 19 of 20 carrying debt, and supply is dispersed, with the largest supplier at about 6% and the top 5 at about 14%. Thirteen borrow USDT and eight borrow USDC against WBTC collateral, so HF in the cohort tracks the BTC price.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the supply cap from 35,500 to 36,000 on Aave V3 Core, which places the reserve at approximately 97.1% post-change supply cap utilization.

USDT (Aave V3 Core)

USDT has reached 97.2% borrow cap utilization (2.49B / 2.56B) on the Aave V3 Core instance.

Borrow Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, November 18, 2026

The top 20 USDT borrowers run health factors between 1.02 and 2.56 with a median of 1.23, and the largest borrower accounts for about 6% of outstanding debt. Collateral behind these positions is mainly ETH assets, with 9 of the 20 posting WETH, 4 wstETH and 3 weETH, alongside a minority posting USDe, sUSDe, syrupUSDT or WBTC, so HF in the cohort largely tracks the ETH price.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the borrow cap from 2.56B to 2.7B on Aave V3 Core, which places the reserve at approximately 92.1% post-change borrow cap utilization. The proposed borrow cap corresponds to 92.2% reserve utilization at current supply, below the 94% optimal point.

Cap Reductions

  • USDC on Aave V3 Core sits at 87.5% borrow cap utilization (2.58B / 2.95B), with borrows down approximately 5% since November 11, 2026 and reserve utilization at 95.8%, above the 94% optimal point. The proposed cap of 2.7B lands at approximately 95.6% post-change cap utilization.
  • USCC on Aave V3 Horizon sits at 16.7% supply cap utilization (1.26M / 7.5M), with supply down 73.8% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 3M lands at approximately 41.9% post-change cap utilization.
  • USTB on Aave V3 Horizon sits at 7.5% supply cap utilization (603,310 / 8M), with supply down 36.7% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 2M lands at approximately 30.2% post-change cap utilization.

Stablecoin IRM Changes

The stablecoin interest rate adjustments proposed by TokenLogic cover 12 Aave V3 reserves. We recommend implementing the Slope 1 increases in 10 BPS steps, with this update moving each reserve 10 BPS toward its proposed target; on the Aave V3 Monad reserves, this step reaches the target. The Slope 1 reduction on EURC on Aave V3 Base, where utilization sits well below the optimal point, and the optimal utilization change on USDC on Aave V3 Base are implemented in full.

These reserves carry approximately 3.55B in aggregate debt, most of it in USDC on Aave V3 Core and USDT0 on Aave V3 Plasma. Slope 2 is unchanged, so where only Slope 1 moves, the borrow rate at and above the optimal point shifts by the full Slope 1 change and the incentive to repay or supply during a liquidity squeeze is preserved. The remaining increases toward each target are to be implemented in further 10 BPS steps.

USDC Optimal Utilization (Aave V3 Base)

USDC on Aave V3 Base holds approximately 185.4M of supply against 170.9M of debt, at 92.2% utilization. Raising the optimal point from 90% to 92% adds approximately 3.7M of borrow capacity at the kink and reduces the liquidity remaining at the kink from approximately 18.5M to 14.8M. The supplier base is dispersed, with the largest supplier holding about 3.8% of supply (approximately 7.0M) and the top 10 about 17.2%, so the liquidity at the new kink exceeds the largest single position.

With utilization just above the current kink, the combined change lowers the borrow rate at current utilization from 6.95% to 5.10%.

Other IRM Changes

USDC IRM (Aave V3 Arbitrum)

USDC on Aave V3 Arbitrum holds approximately 182.4M of supply against 162.3M of debt, at 89.0% utilization. Slope 1 rises from 4.30% to 4.40% and the optimal point from 90% to 92%, which moves the borrow rate at current utilization from 4.25% to 4.26%. Raising the optimal point adds approximately 3.6M of borrow capacity at the kink and reduces the liquidity remaining at the kink from approximately 18.2M to 14.6M. The largest supplier holds about 11.8% of supply (approximately 21.5M) and the top 10 about 55.6%, so the largest single position exceeds the liquidity at both the current and the new kink.

USD₮0 IRM (Aave V3 X Layer)

USD₮0 on Aave V3 X Layer holds approximately 89.6M of supply against 78.1M of debt, at 87.2% utilization. Slope 1 rises from 4.50% to 5.00%, Slope 2 falls from 20.00% to 10.00%, and the optimal point rises from 90% to 92%, which moves the borrow rate at current utilization from 4.36% to 4.74%. Raising the optimal point adds approximately 1.8M of borrow capacity at the kink and reduces the liquidity remaining at the kink from approximately 9.0M to 7.2M. Supply is concentrated, with the largest supplier holding about 56% of supply (approximately 50.1M) and the top 2 about 85%, so a withdrawal by the largest supplier would exceed the liquidity at the kink under both curves.

With the lower Slope 2, the borrow rate at full utilization falls from 24.50% to 15.00%.

USDe Base Rate (Aave V3 Mantle)

The USDe base variable borrow rate on Aave V3 Mantle rises from 6.60% to 7.00%, the base rate applied to USDe on Aave V3 Core, Monad, X Layer, Plasma and Avalanche. Outstanding USDe debt on the instance is negligible, at approximately 0.03% utilization.

Aave V3 Core:

Stablecoin IRM:

  • Increase Slope 1 by 10 BPS on 11 stablecoin reserves across Aave V3 Core, Base, Avalanche, Optimism, Plasma, Monad and Mantle, reduce Slope 1 for EURC on Aave V3 Base from 7.50% to 7.00%, and raise the optimal utilization point for USDC on Aave V3 Base from 90% to 92%.

Other IRM:

  • Increase Slope 1 for USDC on Aave V3 Arbitrum from 4.30% to 4.40% and raise the optimal utilization point from 90% to 92%.
  • For USD₮0 on Aave V3 X Layer, increase Slope 1 from 4.50% to 5.00%, reduce Slope 2 from 20.00% to 10.00%, and raise the optimal utilization point from 90% to 92%.
  • Increase the base variable borrow rate for USDe on Aave V3 Mantle from 6.60% to 7.00%.

WBTC (Aave V3 Core)

WBTC has reached 98.4% supply cap utilization (34,938 / 35,500) on the Aave V3 Core instance.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, November 18, 2026

The top 20 WBTC suppliers run health factors between 1.17 and 6.03 with a median of 1.72, with 19 of 20 carrying debt, and supply is dispersed, with the largest supplier at about 6% and the top 5 at about 14%. Thirteen borrow USDT and eight borrow USDC against WBTC collateral, so HF in the cohort tracks the BTC price.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the supply cap from 35,500 to 36,000 on Aave V3 Core, which places the reserve at approximately 97.1% post-change supply cap utilization.

USDT (Aave V3 Core)

USDT has reached 97.2% borrow cap utilization (2.49B / 2.56B) on the Aave V3 Core instance.

Borrow Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, November 18, 2026

The top 20 USDT borrowers run health factors between 1.02 and 2.56 with a median of 1.23, and the largest borrower accounts for about 6% of outstanding debt. Collateral behind these positions is mainly ETH assets, with 9 of the 20 posting WETH, 4 wstETH and 3 weETH, alongside a minority posting USDe, sUSDe, syrupUSDT or WBTC, so HF in the cohort largely tracks the ETH price.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the borrow cap from 2.56B to 2.7B on Aave V3 Core, which places the reserve at approximately 92.1% post-change borrow cap utilization. The proposed borrow cap corresponds to 92.2% reserve utilization at current supply, below the 94% optimal point.

Cap Reductions

  • USDC on Aave V3 Core sits at 87.5% borrow cap utilization (2.58B / 2.95B), with borrows down approximately 5% since November 11, 2026 and reserve utilization at 95.8%, above the 94% optimal point. The proposed cap of 2.7B lands at approximately 95.6% post-change cap utilization.
  • USCC on Aave V3 Horizon sits at 16.7% supply cap utilization (1.26M / 7.5M), with supply down 73.8% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 3M lands at approximately 41.9% post-change cap utilization.
  • USTB on Aave V3 Horizon sits at 7.5% supply cap utilization (603,310 / 8M), with supply down 36.7% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 2M lands at approximately 30.2% post-change cap utilization.

Stablecoin IRM Changes

The stablecoin interest rate adjustments proposed by TokenLogic cover 12 Aave V3 reserves. We recommend implementing the Slope 1 increases in 10 BPS steps, with this update moving each reserve 10 BPS toward its proposed target; on the Aave V3 Monad reserves, this step reaches the target. USDC on Aave V3 Base holds approximately 185.4M of supply against 170.9M of debt, at 92.2% utilization. The supplier base is dispersed, with the largest supplier holding about 3.8% of supply (approximately 7.0M) and the top 10 about 17.2%, so the liquidity at the new kink exceeds the largest single position.

Raising the optimal point adds approximately 3.6M of borrow capacity at the kink and reduces the liquidity remaining at the kink from approximately 18.2M to 14.6M. The largest supplier holds about 11.8% of supply (approximately 21.5M) and the top 10 about 55.6%, so the largest single position exceeds the liquidity at both the current and the new kink.

governance_posts.description:
title: [Direct-To-AIP] Umbrella Reward Renewal and Parameter Update on Aave V3 Core

author: @TokenLogic

created: 2026-11-20

Overview

The Umbrella reward period for USDC, USDT and WETH on Aave V3 Core ends on December 2, 2026. This proposal extends it to April 2, 2027, renews the Collector allowances and updates the parameters set in TokenLogic’s June parameter update.

Aave V3 Core is being repositioned around established and liquid collateral. The rsETH and osETH loops behind 23% of WETH debt are to migrate to other collateral on Core or to Aave V4, or unwind, and weETH, the largest WETH collateral, no longer carries restaking.

Since the June update, stablecoin stake has remained well above target, while WETH stake has remained below it. We propose raising Target Liquidity from 38.84M to 45.80M USDC and from 40.37M to 45.20M USDT, reflecting half the percentage growth in each loan book since June. The APY at target would fall to 2.50% for both stablecoins, from 3.14% for USDC and 3.17% for USDT. WETH Target Liquidity would remain at 18,716 WETH, with annual emissions unchanged at 470 aEthWETH, until the rsETH and osETH offboarding completes. Annual spend at maximum emission would fall from $3.35M to $3.13M.

All data are as of November 17, 2026. Figures in the tables are rounded to at most two decimals; the Specification gives exact parameter values.

Framework for Umbrella Liquidity Requirements

This proposal applies the framework from TokenLogic’s June parameter update. Target Liquidity follows each market’s loan book, adjusted for collateral quality and the Deficit Offset. The premium follows alternative yields and each module’s stake.

Active Loan Exposure

Borrowing has grown in all three covered markets since the June update. USDC loans rose 36%, USDT loans rose 24%, and WETH loans rose 15% (measured in WETH). Part of the USDC growth is recent and concentrated: in early November, one account collateralized with USDe and sUSDe borrowed more than $330M of USDC within a few hours, while USDT borrowing grew more gradually.


Source: TokenLogic Aave Analytics API | November 17, 2026

Collateral Quality

We measure collateral quality by the pristine share of the collateral behind each market’s debt, with pristine defined as ETH, WBTC, cbBTC, wstETH, USDC and USDT. That share has fallen for both stablecoins and risen for WETH as rsETH left the book.


Source: TokenLogic Aave Analytics API, Ethereum mainnet | June 3 and November 17, 2026


Source: TokenLogic Aave Analytics API | June 3 and November 17, 2026

Two-thirds of the USDC decline comes from USDe and sUSDe, which rose from 4% to 12% of the collateral behind USDC debt, with weETH accounting for most of the rest. Nearly all of the USDe-backed debt sits in stable-on-stable E-Mode loops. In USDT the smaller decline came as weETH and syrupUSDT grew; Core prices syrupUSDT at Maple’s loss-adjusted exit value, and Maple reports no unrealized losses today.

Outside stable-on-stable loops, 1% of USDC debt and 1.3% of USDT debt sit below a health factor of 1.1. If syrupUSDT positions count as credit-bearing, the USDT share is 5.4%, and in both markets collateral covers debt close to twice over.


Source: TokenLogic Aave Analytics API | November 17, 2026

The WETH book remains a leveraged staking book, with weETH at more than half of collateral value. About 94% of WETH debt sits in ETH-correlated E-Mode loops, almost all of it at health factors between 1.01 and 1.06 and exposed to the exchange rate between the liquid staking token and ETH, the risk that materialized in the rsETH incident. In August 2026, ether.fi removed restaking from weETH, which is now a plain liquid staking token with no EigenLayer AVS slashing exposure. This removes one source of risk to the WETH reserve.

The reserves in the repositioning ARFC’s scope back only $68M of USDC debt and $47M of USDT debt, so the repositioning mainly affects WETH. On WETH they back a far larger amount, almost all of it against rsETH and osETH. The ARFC stops new supply and borrowing against osETH and keeps rsETH frozen, as it has been since April. It also adds wstETH, weETH and cbETH to the rsETH E-Mode, so the loops can swap collateral without repaying their WETH debt. The ARFC provides for an orderly migration, worked out with the issuers and largest borrowers, into collateral that remains on Core or into Aave V4.


Source: TokenLogic Aave Analytics API, Aave governance forum | November 17, 2026

Deficit Offsets

This proposal does not resize Deficit Offsets. The USDC offset of 1.3M USDC and the USDT offset of 1.6M USDT, set in April, stand in full ahead of stakers, and no USDC or USDT staker has been slashed since launch. In May the WETH offset was raised above the deficit recorded in the rsETH incident, so no WETH staker was slashed. Net of that deficit, the WETH offset ahead of stakers is 77 WETH. The GHO offset stays at 3 million GHO, on a module that no longer emits.

Relative Yield Environment

Yields on the stablecoin alternatives tracked below have risen since June, and Aave Core supply rates rose with them. Stakers earn those rates through waEthUSDC and waEthUSDT on top of Umbrella emissions. Over the last seven days, annualized total yields averaged 7.0% for USDC stakers and 5.0% for USDT stakers. The lower premium proposed for both stablecoins assumes supply rates stay near current levels.

Lido stETH, weETH and Aave Core WETH supply have stayed close to their June levels, and the WETH Umbrella emission APR on its own sits above both staking yields.


Source: FRED, TokenLogic Aave Analytics API, Morpho, Sky, Ethena, DefiLlama (Maple, Lido, ether.fi) | 7-day averages to June 3 and to November 17, 2026 (SOFR, T-bill and Fed funds to November 16; sUSDe to November 11); Fed funds is the target-range upper bound

Both stablecoin modules have stayed above target every day since the update executed. A staker who starts a cooldown is not committed to leaving. Across all cooldown windows closed since launch (to October 26), stakers withdrew 44% of queued USDC, 55% of queued USDT and 51% of queued WETH (the historical share). If the historical share of today’s USDC queue is withdrawn, USDC stake would stand near 46M, still above target.

Source: Ethereum mainnet (stkwaEthUSDC, stkwaEthUSDT, stkwaEthWETH, Umbrella RewardsController) | November 17, 2026


Source: Ethereum mainnet (Umbrella RewardsController), TokenLogic Aave Analytics API | November 17, 2026

Recommendation

We recommend renewing the Umbrella reward period to April 2, 2027, with new allowances, raising Target Liquidity on USDC and USDT, reducing their APY at target, and keeping WETH Target Liquidity and emissions unchanged.

We propose raising each target by half the percentage growth in its market’s loan book since June, to 45.80M USDC and 45.20M USDT. At the new targets, coverage is 1.77% of USDC loans and 1.83% of USDT loans.

Both modules have maintained stake above target since the update executed in late July, while paying emission yields of 1.47% to 1.83% on USDC and 1.27% to 1.74% on USDT, well below the current APY at target. We therefore propose reducing the APY at target to 2.50%. At today’s stake, the proposed curve pays 1.76% on USDC and 1.53% on USDT.

The main participation risk is the USDT cooldown queue, which contains more than half of stake. Withdrawals at the historical rate would leave USDT stake at 0.91 times the new target, with a proposed emission APR of 2.73%. Withdrawal of the entire queue would leave stake at 0.58 times the target and raise the APR to 3.54%. If the historical share of its queue is withdrawn, USDC stake would fall to 1.01 times its new target, with an emission APR of 2.47%.

The Umbrella reward period for USDC, USDT and WETH on Aave V3 Core ends on December 2, 2026. This proposal extends it to April 2, 2027, renews the Collector allowances and updates the parameters set in TokenLogic’s June parameter update.

Aave V3 Core is being repositioned around established and liquid collateral. The rsETH and osETH loops behind 23% of WETH debt are to migrate to other collateral on Core or to Aave V4, or unwind, and weETH, the largest WETH collateral, no longer carries restaking.

governance_posts.description:
Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V4 reserves.

Aave V4 Ethereum:

  • Increase the add cap for wstETH on the Core Hub Main Spoke from 40K to 60K.
  • Increase the add cap for USDC on the Core Hub Main Spoke from 85M to 110M.
  • Increase the draw cap for USDC on the Core Hub Main Spoke from 60M to 85M.
  • Decrease the add cap for LBTC on the Core Hub Lombard BTC Spoke from 45 to 5.

Aave V4 Avalanche:

  • Increase the add cap for sAVAX on the Core Hub AVAX Correlated Spoke from 1M to 1.5M.

wstETH (Core Hub)

wstETH Main Spoke Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, November 20, 2026

wstETH supply on the Main Spoke is moderately concentrated, with the largest position holding approximately 24% of the reserve, the top three approximately 46%, and the top twenty approximately 84%. All of the top twenty carry debt, mainly USDC and USDG and to a lesser extent USDT and frxUSD, with one position borrowing WETH, at health factors between 1.11 and 5.40 with a median of 1.52, so HF in the cohort tracks mainly the ETH price.

Recommendation

As of November 20, 2026, the wstETH add cap on the Main Spoke is 84.7% utilized (33,868 / 40,000). The proposed add cap of 60K lands at approximately 56.4% post-change add cap utilization.

USDC (Core Hub)

USDC Main Spoke Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, November 20, 2026

USDC supply on the Main Spoke is relatively dispersed, with the largest position holding approximately 10% of the reserve, the top three approximately 18%, and the top twenty approximately 44%.

USDC Main Spoke Borrow Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, November 20, 2026

USDC borrowing on the Main Spoke is moderately concentrated, with the largest position holding approximately 11% of the drawn amount, the top three approximately 29%, and the top twenty approximately 58%. The largest borrowers hold USDC debt mainly against ETH-denominated collateral (wstETH, WETH, and weETH) and BTC-denominated collateral (WBTC, cbBTC, and cirBTC) at health factors between 1.08 and 2.92 with a median of 1.68, so HF in the cohort tracks the ETH and BTC prices.

Recommendation

As of November 20, 2026, the USDC add cap on the Main Spoke is 86.2% utilized (73.29M / 85M) and USDC sits at 90.5% draw cap utilization (54.30M / 60M). The proposed add cap of 110M lands at approximately 66.6% post-change add cap utilization, and the proposed draw cap of 85M at approximately 63.9% post-change draw cap utilization. Further draws are limited by the 6.53M of USDC liquidity available on the Core Hub, where utilization stands at 91.7%.

sAVAX (Avalanche Core Hub)

sAVAX AVAX Correlated Spoke Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, November 20, 2026

sAVAX supply on the AVAX Correlated Spoke is concentrated, with the largest position holding approximately 23% of the reserve, the top three approximately 54%, and the top twenty approximately 97%. Seventeen of the top twenty borrow WAVAX against sAVAX at health factors between 1.00 and 1.54 with a median of 1.12. Since sAVAX is priced through its AVAX exchange rate, HF in the cohort moves with the spread between the sAVAX staking yield and the WAVAX borrow rate.

Recommendation

As of November 20, 2026, the sAVAX add cap on the AVAX Correlated Spoke is 81.9% utilized (819.2K / 1M). The proposed add cap of 1.5M lands at approximately 54.6% post-change add cap utilization.

LBTC (Core Hub)

LBTC on the Lombard BTC Spoke sits at 9.4% add cap utilization (4.22 / 45). The proposed add cap of 5 is approximately 1.18x current supply, landing at approximately 84.5% post-change add cap utilization.

governance_posts.title: Aave V3.8 for integrators: what the reentrancy guard covers and what it leaves open
governance_posts.description:
V3.8 went live on Ethereum Core on 11 November (payload 481 on Ethereum, block 26392162), and POOL_REVISION() now returns 12 on all 16 instances the ARFC listed. Plenty of contracts call the Pool from inside callbacks, so I read the Pool on the feat/V3.8 branch (PR 206, commit aedc9dd) and ran the cases I cared about on a mainnet fork, against the deployed implementation.

What reverts now

Every state-changing entry point takes the lock with nonReentrant: supply, withdraw, borrow, every repay variant, liquidationCall, the collateral and eMode setters (the OnBehalfOf ones too), mintToTreasury and the old deposit. finalizeTransfer is guarded as well, so an aToken transfer can’t settle while another Pool action is running. Liquidations that pay out in aTokens are fine, because transferOnLiquidation moves the balance without going through finalizeTransfer.

flashLoan, flashLoanSimple and rescueTokens only check the lock, they never set it. You can’t start a flash loan from inside another Pool action, but inside executeOperation everything works like in 3.7, which is what AaveLabs said in the ARFC thread. On the fork I supplied USDC from inside a flashLoanSimple callback and it went through.

With a plain ERC-20 underlying, a guarded action has nobody to call back, so most integrations won’t notice anything. To see the new reverts I swapped USDC’s code on the fork for a token that calls back during transferFrom, and supplied it. From inside that hook, flashLoanSimple, mintToTreasury and a zero aUSDC transfer all reverted with ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall, while getUserAccountData returned normally. Gas is up about 550 per guarded call in their own snapshots.

The flash loan window didn’t change

A flash loan never sets the lock, so its callback is as open as before. That’s also where the Pool’s numbers look strange. executeFlashLoanSimple lowers virtualUnderlyingBalance before it calls your receiver, and the rates only get updated when the money comes back (FlashLoanLogic.sol L167-L207).

I flash borrowed all but 1 USDC of the Core USDC reserve. Inside the callback getVirtualUnderlyingBalance returned 1 USDC, and stataUSDC’s maxWithdraw for a holder with about 1.19M USDC of shares returned 0.999999 USDC. After repayment both were back. stataUSDC isn’t wrong here, its maxRedeem caps at the Pool’s virtual balance (ERC4626StataTokenUpgradeable.sol L160-L179), and in that moment the Pool really can’t pay out more.

A vault or router that decides how much to move from those reads, and can run in the same transaction as someone else’s code, can be shown an empty reserve for the price of the flash premium, 5 bps on Core today. You only have to borrow enough to cross whatever threshold it uses, so on a small reserve that’s cheap. It worked the same way in 3.7.

Checking the lock from outside

There’s no public getter, and another contract can’t read the Pool’s transient storage. A staticcall to mintToTreasury with an empty array does the job, the same trick as Balancer’s ensureNotInVaultContext (VaultReentrancyLib.sol L37-L82). The call always fails, because the guard’s TSTORE isn’t allowed in a static call. If the lock is already set it fails one step earlier, with the ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall selector (0x3ee5aeb5) as revert data. Otherwise the revert data is empty. On the fork I got 0x3ee5aeb5 inside the supply hook and empty data outside. I capped the call at 20k gas, since a static call that halts without data burns all the gas you give it.

Inside a flash loan callback the probe says not locked, because nothing is locked there. So a getter wouldn’t have helped with the stataUSDC case above.

Not every instance has it

On 20 November revision 12 shows on Ethereum Core and Lido, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Polygon, Avalanche, BNB, Gnosis, Linea, Mantle, Celo, Plasma, Monad, X Layer and MegaETH. Scroll, Sonic and the EtherFi instance are on 11, zkSync, Metis and Soneium on 10, and Horizon is on 7. The ARFC scoped the rollout to active instances. If one adapter runs on several chains, I’d read POOL_REVISION() per chain rather than assume the guard is there.

If you run a vault or a router on Aave, which Pool reads decide how much you move, and can someone else’s contract be on the call stack when you read them?

governance_posts.content:
V3.8 went live on Ethereum Core on 11 November (payload 481 on Ethereum, block 26392162), and POOL_REVISION() now returns 12 on all 16 instances the ARFC listed. Plenty of contracts call the Pool from inside callbacks, so I read the Pool on the feat/V3.8 branch (PR 206, commit aedc9dd) and ran the cases I cared about on a mainnet fork, against the deployed implementation.

What reverts now

Every state-changing entry point takes the lock with nonReentrant: supply, withdraw, borrow, every repay variant, liquidationCall, the collateral and eMode setters (the OnBehalfOf ones too), mintToTreasury and the old deposit. finalizeTransfer is guarded as well, so an aToken transfer can’t settle while another Pool action is running. Liquidations that pay out in aTokens are fine, because transferOnLiquidation moves the balance without going through finalizeTransfer.

flashLoan, flashLoanSimple and rescueTokens only check the lock, they never set it. You can’t start a flash loan from inside another Pool action, but inside executeOperation everything works like in 3.7, which is what AaveLabs said in the ARFC thread. On the fork I supplied USDC from inside a flashLoanSimple callback and it went through.

With a plain ERC-20 underlying, a guarded action has nobody to call back, so most integrations won’t notice anything. To see the new reverts I swapped USDC’s code on the fork for a token that calls back during transferFrom, and supplied it. From inside that hook, flashLoanSimple, mintToTreasury and a zero aUSDC transfer all reverted with ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall, while getUserAccountData returned normally. Gas is up about 550 per guarded call in their own snapshots.

The flash loan window didn’t change

A flash loan never sets the lock, so its callback is as open as before. That’s also where the Pool’s numbers look strange. executeFlashLoanSimple lowers virtualUnderlyingBalance before it calls your receiver, and the rates only get updated when the money comes back (FlashLoanLogic.sol L167-L207).

I flash borrowed all but 1 USDC of the Core USDC reserve. Inside the callback getVirtualUnderlyingBalance returned 1 USDC, and stataUSDC’s maxWithdraw for a holder with about 1.19M USDC of shares returned 0.999999 USDC. After repayment both were back. stataUSDC isn’t wrong here, its maxRedeem caps at the Pool’s virtual balance (ERC4626StataTokenUpgradeable.sol L160-L179), and in that moment the Pool really can’t pay out more.

A vault or router that decides how much to move from those reads, and can run in the same transaction as someone else’s code, can be shown an empty reserve for the price of the flash premium, 5 bps on Core today. You only have to borrow enough to cross whatever threshold it uses, so on a small reserve that’s cheap. It worked the same way in 3.7.

Checking the lock from outside

There’s no public getter, and another contract can’t read the Pool’s transient storage. A staticcall to mintToTreasury with an empty array does the job, the same trick as Balancer’s ensureNotInVaultContext (VaultReentrancyLib.sol L37-L82). The call always fails, because the guard’s TSTORE isn’t allowed in a static call. If the lock is already set it fails one step earlier, with the ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall selector (0x3ee5aeb5) as revert data. Otherwise the revert data is empty. On the fork I got 0x3ee5aeb5 inside the supply hook and empty data outside. I capped the call at 20k gas, since a static call that halts without data burns all the gas you give it.

Inside a flash loan callback the probe says not locked, because nothing is locked there. So a getter wouldn’t have helped with the stataUSDC case above.

Not every instance has it

On 20 November revision 12 shows on Ethereum Core and Lido, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Polygon, Avalanche, BNB, Gnosis, Linea, Mantle, Celo, Plasma, Monad, X Layer and MegaETH. Scroll, Sonic and the EtherFi instance are on 11, zkSync, Metis and Soneium on 10, and Horizon is on 7. The ARFC scoped the rollout to active instances.
